text:
John initially has 13 LEGO sets. He sells some number of them at $15 each. With the money, he buys 8 video games at $20 each, spending 8 × 20 = $160. He has $5 left, so the total money he received from selling LEGO sets is $160 + $5 = $165. Since each LEGO set sells for $15, the number of sets he sold is 165 ÷ 15 = 11. Therefore, the number of LEGO sets he still has is 13 − 11 = 2.

Answer: 2
reasoning:
We are given: "John plans to sell all his toys and use the money to buy video games. He has 13 lego sets and he sells them for $15 each. He ends up buying 8 video games for $20 each and has $5 left. How many lego sets does he still have?"

Wait: "He plans to sell all his toys" but the question asks "How many lego sets does he still have?" This implies he didn't sell all of them, only some. He has 13 lego sets initially. He sells some number of them for $15 each. With the money, he buys 8 video games at $20 each, total spent = 8 * $20 = $160. He has $5 left. So total money he got from selling some lego sets = $160 + $5 = $165. Since each lego set sells for $15, number of lego sets sold = $165 / $15 = 11. He started with 13, sold 11, so he still has 13 - 11 = 2 lego sets.

Answer: 2
